title: Algebraicity of the stack of finite locally free covers of fixed degree
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $d\geq1$ be an integer. On the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], let $\mathcal C_d(T)$ be the groupoid whose objects are finite locally free morphisms $Z\to T$ of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and whose arrows are $T$-isomorphisms of these schemes. Pullback is scheme base change [def-pc-fibre-product]; an arrow above $T'\to T$ is a cartesian map of the covers. Thus $\mathcal C_d=\mathcal H_d(\operatorname{id}_{h_S})$ in [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids], with $h_S$ the discrete groupoid represented by $S$. Then $\mathcal C_d$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. This holds over arbitrary $S$, without Noetherian or characteristic hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 05YQ (proposition-finite-hilbert-point), criteria.tex; its H_d is C_d over the fixed scheme S.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-unit-framed-algebra-smooth-groupoid] over the given $S$, obtaining $X$, $G$ and the smooth groupoid whose point groupoids are $FA_d$. Its fppf stackification $Q$ is algebraic by [lem-sfb-smooth-groupoid-fppf-quotient]. This applies directly over arbitrary $S$: the arrow space is the scheme $G\times_SX$, and both source and target are smooth. No smoothness of $X/S$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 05YP and the paragraph before Tag 05YQ

proof.text: Define $F:FA_d\to\mathcal C_d$ by $m\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_T(\mathcal O_T^d,m)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec]. On each affine open this is the spectrum of a free rank-$d$ algebra, finite locally free by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum]; on every residue field its vector-space dimension is $d$, so it has degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. These affine tests establish the required local properties on $T$. An arrow labelled $g:m\to m'$ is an algebra map $(\mathcal O_T^d,m')\to(\mathcal O_T^d,m)$, hence gives the scheme arrow $F(m)\to F(m')$. Relative spectrum commutes with arbitrary pullback by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-spec-base-change]; the map on the pulled-back free modules applies the base morphism to the entries of $m$ and $g$. Thus $F$ is a pullback-compatible functor, with the indicated arrow direction.

The functor $F$ is fully faithful on every fibre. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](3) identifies all $T$-isomorphisms between its two relative spectra with algebra isomorphisms in the reverse direction. A map $\mathcal O_T^d\to\mathcal O_T^d$ is determined by the $d$ images of the standard sections, so is exactly a matrix over $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. It is invertible precisely when its inverse is another such matrix. The unit condition is $g(e_1)=e_1$, and compatibility with multiplication is $m'=g^{-1}m(g\otimes g)$. These are precisely the arrows defining $FA_d$, including composition, and the identification respects restriction.

Every cover $p:Z\to T$ is locally in the image of $F$. By [lem-pc-flf-properties], $\mathcal A=p_*\mathcal O_Z$ is locally free of rank $d$, with residue algebra equal to the fibre algebra. At $t\in T$ this algebra has dimension $d>0$, so its unit is nonzero: a zero unit would make the entire algebra zero. Choose an affine neighbourhood where $\mathcal A$ is free and write $1=(u_1,\ldots,u_d)$. Some coordinate $u_j$ is nonzero modulo $t$; shrink to $D(u_j)$. The ordered columns $(1,e_1,\ldots,\widehat{e_j},\ldots,e_d)$ have determinant $\pm u_j$, a unit, hence are a basis with first vector $1$. In this basis multiplication is a commutative associative bilinear law with unit $e_1$, an object of $FA_d$. The map $p$ is affine since it is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The anti-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] therefore identifies $Z$ with the relative spectrum of this algebra. These neighbourhoods cover $T$ and are fppf coverings [def-pc-fppf-site].

source.place: Tag 05YQ, check (2); determinant argument for the unit-adapted basis

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-hilbert-stack-descent] with $F=\operatorname{id}_{h_S}$, $\mathcal C_d$ is an fppf stack. Extend the functor of step 2 to $\bar F:Q\to\mathcal C_d$ using [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. For two objects of $Q$, choose a common fppf cover on which both come from $FA_d$. On this cover step 3 identifies their isomorphism sheaves: in $Q$ they are the sheafification of the $FA_d$ isomorphism presheaves, which step 3 identifies with the already-sheaves in $\mathcal C_d$. Hence the local identification glues to an identification globally. Thus $\bar F$ is fully faithful. Step 4 gives local lifts of any $\mathcal C_d$ object to $Q$. Full faithfulness lifts their overlap comparisons uniquely; their cocycle equations follow from uniqueness. Stack descent in $Q$ glues these lifts, and descent of the comparison arrows in $\mathcal C_d$ gives an isomorphism of its image with the prescribed object. Thus $\bar F$ is essentially surjective as well. The equivalence $Q\simeq\mathcal C_d$ transfers the representable diagonal and smooth surjective atlas furnished in step 1, so $\mathcal C_d$ is algebraic [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack].
